- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–14 day window and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 18-day moving average as a smoothing anchor for long-term bias correction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often predicts minor drift; assume 0.5–1% mean reversion toward prior 14-day average.
- Avoid forecasting price jumps >10% from recent peak unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.8) — such moves are often overestimated and followed by correction.
